title: Musa
question: What does it take to stand before a tyrant, and then lead a freed people?
intro: Musa (Moses) is named in the Quran more often than any other prophet. His life runs from a river to a palace, a desert, a fire on a mountain and a sea split in two. He faced Pharaoh, the Quran's clearest picture of a tyrant, and then the long work of guiding a freed people who often doubted.

His story also carries the stories of his community: the covenant at the mountain, the calf, the cow they argued over, and Qarun, ruined by pride in his wealth. Later comes a town that broke the Sabbath (7:163). The Quran tells all this to the Prophet ﷺ and his followers as a mirror: freedom is a gift, and a covenant is a trust to keep.

passages.context: Pharaoh was killing the newborn sons of the Children of Israel (28:4).
passages.point: A mother is told to do the unthinkable and given two promises: he will return to her, and he will be a messenger. 28:13 shows the first kept.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Musa and his brother Harun (Aaron) are sent to Pharaoh, who claimed "I am your most exalted lord" (79:24).
passages.point: Even to a tyrant, the command is gentle speech, in the hope that he may remember. The method is mercy, not contempt.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Pharaoh's army pursues the Israelites to the sea at sunrise (26:60).
passages.point: Trapped, his people panic. Musa answers with certainty, "with me is my Lord", and the sea parts like towering mountains.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Addressed to the Children of Israel in the Prophet's ﷺ time, recalling their ancestors' covenant.
passages.point: The covenant's core: worship Allah alone, do good to parents, relatives, orphans and the needy, speak well, pray and give zakah. The verse notes that a few kept it.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: While Musa was away for forty nights (7:142), the Samiri cast the people's ornaments into the fire (20:87).
passages.point: A lowing calf is hailed as "your god". The Quran asks how anything that cannot speak, harm or benefit could be worshipped.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Qarun was "from the people of Moses", a man of immense wealth.
passages.point: His own people warn him not to exult. He credits his wealth to his own knowledge (28:78), and the earth swallows him and his home (28:81).
passages.label: stated

visual.title: The life of Musa
visual.label: explained
visual.caption: The order follows the Quran's accounts and common scholarly reading. The Quran does not say when in his life the cow or Qarun came, so they are marked undated.

items.label: The river
items.text: His mother sets him afloat; Pharaoh's household takes him in.

items.label: A fatal blow
items.text: He strikes a man who dies, repents, and flees.

items.label: Shelter and marriage
items.text: He waters two women's flocks; years of work and marriage.

items.label: The fire on the mount
items.text: Allah speaks to him and sends him to Pharaoh.

items.label: The magicians
items.text: Their tricks are swallowed; they fall down believing.

items.label: The sea
items.text: The sea parts; Israel crosses and Pharaoh's army drowns.

items.label: Forty nights
items.text: The Tablets are given; Harun leads in his place.

items.label: The calf
items.text: The Samiri's calf; Musa returns angry and grieved.

items.label: The covenant
items.text: The mount raised over them: take the Torah firmly.

items.label: Forty years
items.text: Refusing to enter the land, they wander.

items.label: The cow
items.text: Told to slaughter a cow, they question and delay.

items.label: Qarun
items.text: The proud rich man is swallowed by the earth.

word.meaning: A firm covenant, a binding pledge
word.nuance: From a root meaning to tie fast and to trust. The same root gives "the most trustworthy handhold" (2:256). The Quran uses mīthāq for the pledge with the Children of Israel (2:83), the covenant taken from the prophets (33:7), and even marriage, "a solemn covenant" (4:21).

mixup.truth: In the Quran's account, the Samiri made the calf (20:85-88). Harun warned the people, "you are only being tested by it... follow me" (20:90), but they refused until Musa returned. When Musa seized him, Harun explained he had feared dividing the people (20:94). The Quran clears Harun of the idol.

remember: Musa is the prophet named most often in the Quran; his story runs from the river to the parted sea.
Even Pharaoh was to be addressed with gentle speech (20:44).
The covenant's core: worship Allah alone, kindness to family and the needy, good speech, prayer and zakah (2:83).

quiz.q: How were Musa and Harun told to speak to Pharaoh?
quiz.why: 20:44: "And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allah]."

quiz.q: In the Quran's account, who made the calf the people worshipped?
quiz.why: 20:85-88 name the Samiri. Harun had warned the people against it (20:90).

quiz.q: What did the magicians do when Musa's staff swallowed what they had made?
quiz.why: 20:70: they said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses." Even Pharaoh's threats did not move them (20:71-72).

reflect: Alone and far from home, Musa told Allah, "I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need" (28:24). What would you ask for if you prayed that today?
